Translate a model's `ini()` priors into Stan

Source: R/stanPriors.R
stanPriors.Rd

Consumes [rxode2::rxUiPriors()] and [lotri::lotriPriorDists()] and returns the Stan-side pieces: per-parameter bound declarations (support-promoted) and sampling statements for population parameters, and the classified omega-block priors for the model generator.

Usage

stanPriors(ui)

Arguments

ui

an rxode2 ui (or model function)

Value

a list:

pop

data.frame over population-parameter priors: `name` (nlmixr2), `par` (Stan identifier), `prior`, `stanName`, `kind`, `lower`, `upper` (effective, support-promoted), `constraint`, `truncated`, `members` (comma-joined for a multivariate group, `NA` otherwise), `statement`

omega

data.frame over omega-block priors: `name`, `neta1`, `neta2`, `prior`, `stanName`, `kind`

Author

Matthew L Fidler

Examples

# priors are read from the model's ini({}) block, and map one-to-one
# onto Stan's distributions
mod <- function() {
  ini({
    tcl <- 1
    tv <- 3
    add.sd <- 0.5
    prior(tcl) ~ dnorm(0, 10)
    prior(add.sd) ~ dcauchy(0, 5)
    eta.cl ~ 0.1
  })
  model({
    cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl)
    v <- exp(tv)
    cp <- linCmt()
    cp ~ add(add.sd)
  })
}
p <- stanPriors(rxode2::rxode2(mod))
#>  
#>  
#> ℹ parameter labels from comments are typically ignored in non-interactive mode
#> ℹ Need to run with the source intact to parse comments
p$pop$statement
#> [1] "tcl ~ normal(0, 10);"   "add_sd ~ cauchy(0, 5);"
